intro: CLAUDE.md is the single most impactful thing you can do to improve Claude Code's output quality. It's read automatically at the start of every session.

sections.code:
# Project: [Name]

## Overview
[1–2 sentences: what this is and what it does]
Stack: Next.js 14, TypeScript, Prisma, PostgreSQL

## Commands
```bash
npm run dev          # start dev server (port 3000)
npm test             # jest — run all tests
npm run lint         # eslint + prettier check
npm run typecheck    # tsc --noEmit
npm run build        # production build
npm run db:migrate   # run pending Prisma migrations
```

## Architecture
```
src/
  app/          Next.js app router pages
  components/   React components (named exports only)
  lib/          Shared utilities and helpers
  api/          API route handlers
prisma/
  schema.prisma DB schema
```

## Conventions
- TypeScript strict mode — no `any`
- Named exports everywhere, no default exports
- All DB queries via `lib/db.ts` — never import Prisma directly
- API routes return `{ data }` on success, `{ error: string }` on failure
- Zod for all API input validation

## What NOT to Do
- Never use `any` — use `unknown` and narrow
- Never commit `.env` or `.env.local`
- Never write `console.log` in production code

items.title: Update it with decisions
items.body: When you make an architectural decision, add it. CLAUDE.md should reflect how the codebase is actually built, not how you planned it.

items.title: Keep it honest
items.body: Wrong conventions are worse than no conventions. Claude will follow what's written — if it's outdated, you'll get outdated code.

items.title: One line per rule
items.body: Dense lists are read; paragraphs are skimmed. Be terse. 'Use dayjs not date-fns' beats a paragraph about date handling.

items.title: Add gotchas
items.body: Non-obvious constraints ('we use dayjs not date-fns', 'never import Prisma directly') are the most valuable content. Obvious things don't need to be said.
